content: STAGE 1 (scoping pass over the four proposals against the contract). Goal: check which candidates satisfy behaviour + explicit curvature + real one-pathway coupling + switchable testable effect + minimal spec, before any ranking. Read: the four proposals (OCCURV-FIELD-RQ f40daafe155f3be3, RSPC-RQ 1e3482d1228219f6, parentcurv-rq-2026 ba8fb09c35ebc869, OCCURVE-RQ 8a7a312e13d89a7e) and the shared frozen bundle items E5-E13. Observations: (a) all four share the same observed evidence base, so no candidate owns unique outcome evidence - their own figures are hypotheses, not measurements; (b) FIELD, parentcurv and OCCURVE make the metric/cell scale a function of a measured behaviour statistic (strongest coupling form); RSPC keeps fixed c=-1 and adds a row-normalised successor-code log-prior inside the same geodesic score (coupling exists but geometry does not respond to behaviour); (c) OCCURVE's key radius formula is never written (R_ref and g undefined) and its curvature is trainable with a 1e-3 floor that admits a Euclidean run, so the coupling cannot be verified from the spec; (d) parentcurv fixes level-1 curvature to exactly 1 (no tuned constant) but removes the radial mechanism that produced the GEOCAP l1 gain and omits the clamp needed to keep 1-c|z|^2 positive at c=4; (e) FIELD has derived curvature range [kappa_max/e, kappa_max]=[0.645,1.754] from the c*=0.9 shell clamp and its per-codeword task was checked by hand: at fixed coordinates the geodesic distance strictly increases with kappa (0.645->1.169 vs 1.754->1.514 at ||x||=||c||=0.5), so raising kappa on low-reach hoarding codewords does shed items (sign is correct), but it compares distances from different curvatures in one argmin and its spec text is truncated at the decode line. Open: ordering of the top two (both in scope, different risk profiles).

STAGE 2 (evidence grounding of the ordering). Goal: tie each placement to a specific bundle item rather than to prose. Read: E5, E6, E7, E8, E9, E10, E11. Observations used: E6 (width-20 beam) shows the loss of recall is at depth 4 - gold prefix alive at depth 4 is 0.068-0.088 across all arms while depth-1 survives at 1.000 for most, and the best arm (resample) reaches recall@10 0.06363, i.e. below the 0.065 target; E8 shows K=256 leaves only 0.0822 of canonical pairs sharing a first-level cluster (K=16 gives 0.3106), so behavioural concentration/capacity at the deep levels is the measured bottleneck, not the encoder; E5 shows per-item behaviour is strongly stratified (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 low-entropy vs 0.0543 high, Spearman -0.973), so per-item/per-codeword behaviour statistics are informative; E10 shows 115582 distinct train edges, density 5.33, mean out-degree 5.45, enough for a K x K pair table and for per-codeword occupancy aggregates; E9 shows the train-only behavioural signal is real but modest (positive shares successor cohort 0.9291 vs 0.8871 negatives) which argues for bounded tilts rather than large behaviour-driven offsets. Reasoning: RSPC-RQ acts on the observed depth-3/4 prefix-predictability bottleneck with a row-mean-1 prior (bounded), measured beta/tau, no per-codeword demand growth, and keeps the curved Mobius residual subtraction in the same pathway -> rank 1. OCCURV-FIELD-RQ has the strongest coupling (behaviour becomes the metric) and a derived bounded curvature range plus residual renormalisation that directly answers the level-3 capacity loss, but mixed-curvature argmin and truncated spec are unproven -> rank 2. parentcurv-rq-2026 has a clean no-tuning level-1 (kappa=1) and correct negative-feedback sign but puts level 1 into a curved metric, discarding the radial mechanism behind valid_l1_hard_er 3.885, and lacks the ball-boundary clamp -> rank 3. OCCURVE-RQ is grounded (successor entropy is the best-evidenced signal) but its central formula is missing and its curvature may legally drift to Euclidean -> rank 4. Open: none; final answer written next.

STAGE 3 (final answer, complete). One mechanism per the rank-2026-10-v1 policy; no ablation arm is required by any placement, all placements are single-run capable. FINAL ANSWER:

grounded behaviour, ungrounded specification, hence last."}], "objection": "RSPC-RQ's behaviour term is an additive, fixed-curvature log-prior on the geodesic score, so the geometry never responds to behaviour; if the derived 1/ln K tilt is far too weak the single run degenerates into a plain curved residual quantiser with the GEOCAP-era level-3 risk, and with no geometry-off or behaviour-off arm trained there is no way to tell after the fact which regime the one run was in."}
